Article Title: PM Modi inaugurates global conference on environment, climate dynamics
Article Text:
The conference is being held on September 19 and 20

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated a two-day international conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”, organised by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi.The conference, being held on September 19 and 20, brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from India and abroad. Judicial representatives from 17 countries are also participating in the event.Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav, Attorney General R Venkataramani and NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava attended the inaugural session.The conference will feature four technical sessions focusing on key environmental and climate-related issues. According to the NGT, the discussions will examine major challenges facing the world, identify gaps in policy-making and implementation, and explore ways to strengthen institutional cooperation.The event also aims to facilitate the exchange of successful environmental practices and strengthen environmental justice amid growing challenges linked to climate change, development and governance.President Droupadi Murmu will attend the valedictory session on Sunday. Union minister Manohar Lal, Supreme Court judge Justice PS Narasimha, NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta are also scheduled to attend the concluding session.The conference is expected to work towards developing a roadmap for addressing present and future environmental and climate challenges.
Article Summary: The conference is being held on september 19 and 20 at vigyan bhawan in new delhi. It brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from india and abroad. Judicial representatives from 17 countries are also participating in the event.

Article Title: ‘PNS Hunain violated maritime norms’: India rejects Pakistan’s ‘usual prevarication’ over naval collision
Article Text:
India rejects Pakistan’s claims after INS Kolkata collision with PNS Hunain

What happened in the Arabian Sea

NEW DELHI: India on Friday rejected Pakistan’s allegations over the collision between Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata and Pakistan Navy vessel PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea, accusing Islamabad of trying to “hide the truth” and saying the Pakistani vessel violated a 1991 bilateral agreement and international maritime regulations.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's response to India's diplomatic protest was expected and rejected the allegations against India."Recent events involving Pakistan and India have taken place. I would like to clarify a few things before you. We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest lodged by us. As always, it is an evasive reply or an attempt to hide the truth, which was expected from them. We completely reject the allegations made against us. I would like to place some facts before you and reiterate them. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when a Pakistani naval ship, PNS Hunain, behaved in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea, resulting in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was a grave violation of Article 10 of the Agreement on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers, and Troop Movements between India and Pakistan of April 1991.This article explicitly states that naval units in the sea should not come within three nautical miles of each other..."Jaiswal said the Pakistani vessel's manoeuvre also violated international maritime rules governing the prevention of collisions at sea."We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest we had lodged. It is the usual prevarication that we expected. We reject the allegations and insinuations contained therein. Let me reiterate the facts of the matter for you. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when Pakistani naval ship Hunain conducted itself in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea that resulted in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was in gross violation of Article 10 of the Agreement Between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers and Troop Movements of 1991, which clearly specifies that naval units at sea are not to be within three nautical miles of each other. In addition, the Pakistani ship also infringed the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea. The Pakistani side has once again been advised about the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents. The incident did not cause any major damage to INS Kolkata, and she remains at sea..."The collision took place on September 15 in the North Arabian Sea. India has said INS Kolkata was on routine deployment in international waters when PNS Hunain carried out a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre that resulted in the collision.Pakistan, however, has disputed India's account and accused the Indian warship of carrying out aggressive manoeuvres near its naval vessel. Islamabad has also claimed that the incident occurred within Pakistan's exclusive economic zone during its SEASPARK-26 naval exercise.Both countries have lodged diplomatic protests following the incident.Under Article 10 of the 1991 agreement between India and Pakistan, naval units at sea are required to maintain a separation of at least three nautical miles.India has maintained that PNS Hunain came close to INS Kolkata at high speed before the collision, describing the manoeuvre as a violation of the bilateral agreement as well as the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.India also said the incident did not cause major damage to INS Kolkata and that the warship remains at sea. Reports said PNS Hunain suffered damage and subsequently returned to port.
Article Summary: India rejects pakistan’s claims after ins kolkata collision with pns hunain. India accuses islamabad of trying to “hide the truth” and saying the pakistani vessel violated a 1991 bilateral agreement and international maritime regulations. Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said pakistan's response to india's diplomatic protest was expected.

Wanjun Xie, chairman of the China Democratic Party, has claimed in a post on X that Chinese president Xi Jinping fainted during the Brics summit hosted by New Delhi and was taken back to China on a special flight for medical treatment.Xie claimed that after receiving emergency treatment from his accompanying medical team, Xi ended his visit to India early and returned to China on a special plane.According to the post, upon the plane's arrival at Beijing airport, authorities did not arrange for a large group of officials to greet Xi or organise a welcome ceremony. Instead, "a military helicopter was used to transport Xi Jinping directly to Beijing's 301 Hospital for emergency treatment."Xie further claimed that an expert team at Beijing's 301 Hospital diagnosed Xi with "a severe ischemic stroke, that is, a transient cerebral infarction."The post also claimed that Xi "feared that the Indian side might obtain information about his health" and therefore "refused emergency treatment at an Indian hospital" before returning to Beijing for care.According to Xie, "During the flight, as there were no conditions for surgery, the medical team could only administer conservative treatment to sustain Xi Jinping's life."He further claimed that Xi "missed the golden window for emergency care and surgery."The post alleged that even if Xi undergoes surgery at Beijing's 301 Hospital, "there is a high likelihood of severe sequelae."Xie also claimed that "the Beijing authorities are still unable to confirm whether Xi Jinping can recover his health before the visit to the United States", adding that authorities were waiting to determine whether it would be necessary to cancel Xi's planned late-September trip to the US.The post on X also carried Community Notes. NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backed Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that "running a UPI system" is not cheap.While talking to reporters, Omar said that people don't appreciate what they "get for free.""Not everyone is charged. First of all, person-to-person money transfers are not charged. After that, individual consumers will not be charged unless they cross a certain ceiling limit. As far as I understand, running this UPI system is not cheap. It takes a lot of money to run it. And the truth is, we don't properly appreciate what we get for free," J&K CM said."The government should ensure that the general public is not charged these fees. If a company is charged, I have no objection because companies make good money through UPI anyway," he added.This comes after the opposition raised concerns over the rollout of UPI charges, alleging that the cost would ultimately be borne by common citizens.Earlier on Wednesday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi targeted the centre and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of putting a on every single person by “taxing UPI".“Modiji has a completely diff concept, he's neither left or right he has decided to completely lie down straight and in front of Donald Trump. He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving huge amount op money to the United States,” the former Congress president added.The new MDR will take effect from October 15. However, UPI payments between individuals, including transfers made to friends, will not be charged, according to the Centre.Responding to the critics and concerns over the new framework, the Union finance ministry said banks were asked to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. “UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges".

Article Title: ‘Happens all the time alas’: Shashi Tharoor after user flags grammar goof up in PM Modi birthday wish

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday acknowledged a grammatical error in his birthday greeting for Prime Minister Narendra Modi after an X user pointed out his mistake.Tharoor had extended his birthday wishes to Modi on Thursday. However, in his message, the Thiruvananthapuram MP wrote “in his 76th birthday” instead of the grammatically correct phrase “on his 76th birthday”. The error quickly caught the attention of social media users, with one X user calling out the Congress leader over the wording.The Congress leader, who is known for his command of the English language and use of complex vocabulary, responded to the criticism the following day. An X user had highlighted the error, writing, “Shashi ji made a grammar mistake !!! even if it is fat finger !!!”Acknowledging the mistake, Tharoor replied, “Yea “on” his birthday became “in”. This happens all the time alas.”The grammar-related exchange comes after Tharoor faced criticism last month over his use of the word “drama” in a post about the flash floods in Nepal.The Congress leader had expressed concern over the disaster after arriving in Kathmandu, where he said he learned about the loss of life and the fact that around 2,000 or more people were estimated to be missing.In his initial post on X, Tharoor wrote, “Took off for Kathmandu yesterday, blissfully unaware of the drama that had taken place in the hills and caused such catastrophic damage.”The reference to the disaster as “drama” drew criticism from social media users, with some questioning the choice of words given the severity of the situation.One user wrote, “Drama?? You are a wordsmith, and this is what you came up with?”Another user asked, “Sir, you are Shakespeare of Indian English. Is the usage of the word DRAMA in the second sentence of the first para appropriate?”Tharoor subsequently explained that he had used the word in a different sense, referring to a situation involving conflicting forces, while also acknowledging that the wording could be misinterpreted."For all those fulminating in outrage about my use of the word 'drama' in my first tweet from Nepal, the word does not only mean something theatrical. It is also defined as 'a state, situation or series of events involving intensely clashing forces'," the Thiruvananthapuram MP said on X.
Article Summary: Shashi tharoor acknowledges grammar error in pm modi birthday wish on x. Congress leader had extended his birthday wishes to modi on thursday. In his message, the thiruvananthapuram mp wrote “in his 76th birthday’ instead of the grammatically correct phrase “on his 76st birthday”

Article Title: Scottish Sikh gets bail in 7 NIA cases after 8 years behind bars
Article Text:
British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who was granted bail

NEW DELHI/LONDON/BATHINDA: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF), taking note of his “long period of incarceration” and acquittal in one of the cases. News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists who have been campaigning for his release.His brother Gurpreet Singh Johal, a solicitor in Dumbarton, where Johal’s wife Gurpreet Kaur Johal also lives, said, “The past two years have been an expensive rollercoaster, contesting bails at Supreme Court and back to the high court in India. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison. We have waited so long and fought so hard for this moment. Whenever evidence against Jagtar is tested in court, judges find what we’ve said all along, which is that there isn’t any. ”Johal’s MP Douglas McAllister, who has been campaigning for his release, described the news as “amazing”. “Now it’s time to bring him home.”Scotland-born Johal, arrested shortly after his 2017 wedding, was named as an accused in eight cases of attempted murder in Punjab and booked by NIA under UAPA.He was acquitted in one of the cases last year.HC heard Johal’s bail appeals in the remaining seven case together Friday and said, “We find the appellant has remained in custody for more than eight years… Only 40 witnesses have so far been examined and we are informed there are another 123 witnesses whose testimony is yet to be recorded... Trial is certainly not likely to conclude any time soon.”On NIA’s claim Johal was a flight risk as a foreign national, HC ordered Johal to surrender his passport and barred him from joining any WhatsApp group or other social media platform where anti-national material was uploaded or circulated or propagated.It rejected NIA’s claim certain witnesses alleged they were threatened and that, if released, Johal might influence the trial.NIA’s cases against Johal arise from a series of allegedly targeted murders and attempted murders in Ludhiana and Jalandhar in 2016-2017. Two cases pertain to the killing of Amit Sharma, president of Shri Hindu Takhat in Ludhiana in Jan 2017, and the attempted murder of Jagdish Kumar Gagneja, RSS vice-president in Punjab, in Jalandhar in Aug 2016.The probe was transferred from Punjab Police to NIA after the offences were identified to be a part of a “transnational conspiracy”. NIA accused Johal of being an “active member” of the “terrorist gang” KLF.Gurpreet Singh Johal told BBC News, “We are still waiting for the order and a report. We expect he won’t be allowed to leave India without permission... But at last we see some light at the end of the tunnel that he will be at least at liberty.”Noting Johal was acquitted of all charges in one case, he said, “Jagtar is innocent and is arbitrarily detained. There is a lot more that has to be done from UK govt. They have not done enough.”Dan Dolan, deputy executive director of Reprieve, a UK legal rights organisation campaigning for Johal’s release, said, “While this judgment is welcome as Jagtar should not be in prison a day longer, we must now watch closely to ensure this order is actually implemented and not obstructed in any way.”Chris Esdaile, senior legal adviser at REDRESS, a London NGO that pursues legal claims on behalf of survivors of torture around the world that also campaigned for Johal, said, “This is a welcome development but it can’t undo the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention without a fair and timely resolution.”
Article Summary: Delhi hc on friday granted bail to british citizen jagtar singh johal. He is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to khalistan liberation force (klf) news of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in dumbarton, scotland. They have not done enough.

Article Title: Uri centre meant for cross-LOC trade will be border tourism hub
Article Text:
TFC will now be used for border tourism

SRINAGAR: A trade facilitation centre (TFC) at Salamabad in border town Uri, which once facilitated duty-free, cashless barter trade between J&K and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), will now be used for border tourism, ending speculation about resumption of trade through the route.A senior tourism department official confirmed the govt had authorised the department to utilise the TFC located in Baramulla district for tourism-related activities. “The larger objective is to use Salamabad as a gateway to the wider Uri border tourism circuit,” the official said. He added that the emphasis will be on “regulated, responsible and curated border tourism”, ensuring that these remain fully aligned with security and administrative requirements.Salamabad TFC, around 100 km north of Srinagar, was originally established for cross-LoC trade. Following the suspension of such trade in 2019, the facility has remained unutilised for its original purpose.After improved relations in 2008, both India and Pakistan decided to allow cross-LoC trade and travel on certain conditions as part of confidence-building measures (CBMs). However, in April 2019, the Centre suspended the facilities saying the trade routes were being misused for funneling illegal weapons, narcotics, and fake currency.“During ongoing investigations of certain cases by NIA, it has been brought out that a significant number of trading concerns engaged in LoC trade are operated by persons closely associated with banned terrorist organisations involved in fuelling terrorism/separatism,” a Union home ministry (MHA) release had said then. The statement also mentioned that some individuals, who had crossed over and joined terror outfits, had opened trading firms in Pakistan.The cross-LoC travel (bus service) and trade were seen as two of the biggest CBMs between the neighbours in decades. Then PM Manmohan Singh flagged off Karwaan-e-Aman (peace caravan), the first cross-LoC bus service that connected Srinagar with Muzaffarabad in PoK, on April 7, 2005.Cross-LoC barter trade began on Oct 21, 2008, through two routes -- Salamabad (Uri)-Muzaffarabad (PoK) and Poonch-Rawalakot (PoK). Traders on either side were permitted to exchange 21 mutually agreed items.Both sides constructed TFCs 5km inside LoC. In J&K, one TFC came up at Salamabad and the other at Chakan da bagh in Jammu’s Poonch district. Trade was allowed through both routes four days a week.
Article Summary: Salamabad tfc, around 100 km north of srinagar, was originally established for cross-loc trade. Following the suspension of such trade in 2019, the facility has remained unutilised. The emphasis will be on ‘regulated, responsible and curated border tourism’

Article Title: Punjab govt announces 8 pc DA hike for employees, pensioners
Article Text:

CHANDIGARH: Ending a prolonged standoff with state employees, the Bhagwant Mann government on Friday announced relief for around eight lakh employees and pensioners, increasing the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 8 per cent.The decision followed a meeting held here between chief minister Bhagwant Mann and representatives of employee and pensioners' organisations.Ministers Aman Arora and Baljeet Kaur, chief secretary KAP Sinha, secretary general administration KK Yadav and others were also present.After the meeting, Gurnam Singh Virk, president of Punjab State Ministerial Services Union, said the enhanced DA will be given from October 1.He said, regarding various other issues, the government has also assured them that these will be discussed soon.The deadlock began August 27 when over three lakh government employees went on a statewide strike by availing mass casual leave, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including release of their pending 18 per cent Dearness Allowance.An official statement quoting Bhagwant Mann said the move reflects his government's commitment to the welfare and dignity of employees, whom he described as the backbone of the state's administrative machinery.The chief minister also announced compulsory monthly meetings with employee representatives to address genuine issues, postings for women employees within 40 kilometres of their homes, and highlighting that around 70,000 government jobs have been provided through a transparent and corruption-free process.Women employees should not have to choose between their career and their family responsibilities. The state government will ensure that the system remains sensitive to their genuine needs, he said.Mann met representatives of employees and pensioners, heard their concerns, it said.After the meeting, Mann stated on X: "Had a very positive meeting today with employee and pensioner organisations. Employees are an important part of our family, and keeping their welfare in mind, we have immediately decided to increase the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 8 per cent. This increase will start reflecting with the October salary"."We also discussed long-pending issues inherited from previous governments, including the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), salary during the probation period, and issues concerning ASHA and Mid-Day Meal workers. We will meet again in the first week of October to work towards a permanent resolution of these longstanding issues."There is no distance between our government and employees. We will resolve every issue through mutual dialogue. We will continue to work together for Punjab's progress," he said.Emphasising that the welfare, dignity and legitimate concerns of government employees remain a priority for his government, Mann said, "As per the decision, two instalments of 4 per cent each will be released to employees and pensioners, with the benefit to be reflected in their salaries from October 1. Ahead of the festive season, this decision will provide additional financial support to thousands of government employees and pensioners and their families. "The chief minister said, "The government understands the responsibilities shouldered by its employees and the pressures they face in their personal and professional lives.""A happy employee is a productive employee and I believe that when an employee works with satisfaction, dignity and peace of mind, the entire system performs better and the people receive better services..."."The state government has an open mind towards the genuine demands of employees and pensioners and these issues will be examined sympathetically and in accordance with the applicable rules, financial implications and legal position."He said the government will examine various long-pending demands, including "the demand for a 2.59 pension multiplication factor, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), restoration of various allowances, implementation of Assured Career Progression (ACP), issues relating to the 2015 and 2020 letters concerning the probation period, generalization of court decisions and others.""No genuine issue concerning employees is being ignored and the government will examine each matter with an open and sympathetic approach. Employee welfare cannot be treated as a one-time exercise and requires continuous dialogue between the government and its workforce," he said.Notably, earlier, the employees had remained adamant on their demand for clearance of DA arrears as per directions of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.The Punjab government had moved the Supreme Court challenging the High Court order directing it to release all pending DA and dearness relief dues to state employees and pensioners within a fortnight, contending that the direction to pay arrears totalling around Rs 14,191 crore in such a short period was impossible.
Article Summary: The decision followed a meeting held here between chief minister bhagwant mann and representatives of employee and pensioners' organisations. The deadlock began august 27 when over three lakh government employees went on a statewide strike by availing mass casual leave, pressing the state government to accept their various demands.

Article Title: 'Will take all necessary actions': India's stern warning amid reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 bilateral pacts
Article Text:
EA breaks silence on reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 pacts

NEW DELHI: India on Friday said it would take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests after reports that Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding signed with New Delhi during the previous Awami League government.Responding to news agency ANI, at the ministry of external affairs’ bi-weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said New Delhi had not received any formal communication from Dhaka on the review.“We also have seen some media reports on this matter, but nothing has been conveyed to us officially. Obviously, India will take all necessary actions to protect its interests,” Jaiswal said.Bangladesh’s ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has said the agreements are being examined with the country’s national interests in mind. chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni said last week, “We are reviewing the agreements that mean 101 MoUs and you will get its (review) result soon.”The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports, connectivity and other bilateral projects. Dhaka has not announced a blanket cancellation of the agreements.The developments come as India-Bangladesh ties face scrutiny over trade, transit, energy, border management and water-sharing issues. India has previously extended more than $7 billion through Lines of Credit for infrastructure projects in Bangladesh, while bilateral arrangements have also enabled the movement of Indian cargo through Bangladeshi ports.Water-sharing remains another key issue. The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is due to expire in December 2026, while the long-pending Teesta agreement remains unresolved.On Friday, Jaiswal said existing mechanisms for discussions on shared rivers remained operational.“In the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, we have the Joint Rivers Commission mechanism to discuss all water-related issues. Technical-level meetings on water matters continue to be held,” he said.India and Bangladesh share 54 rivers, Jaiswal said, adding that water-related issues are handled through the Joint Rivers Commission and other established bilateral mechanisms.The review of the 101 agreements is now expected to provide a clearer indication of whether Dhaka intends to retain, amend or renegotiate specific arrangements.
Article Summary: India says it will take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests. Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding. The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister sheikh hasina’s awami league government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of chattogram and mongla ports.

Article Title: Houthis, Saudis, Iran - and the future of Middle Eastern oil
Article Text:
Houthi fighters stand in front of what they say is a downed Saudi jet, at a location given as Yemen

What’s the latest Houthi offensive all about?

Why is this a serious headache?

Why now?

Why are Saudis in a jam?

What are the takeaways?

In a lightning offensive last week, Yemen’s Houthis took over much of the country’s Red Sea coast, threatening shipping in the vital sea lane that had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade, although a 2022 UN-brokered truce halted their attacks on Saudi territory. But the Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark, adding another front to the wider US-Israel war against Iran. Here’s the lowdown on why the Houthis’ Red Sea threat matters, how this puts Saudi Arabia in a serious pickle, and what it means for the Iran war:The offensive saw Houthis take over key parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast. This adds weight to the Houthi threat to shipping in the vital sea lane. In fact, Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of Saudi ships in the region. Now they can seriously enforce this. Their mere presence along the coastline will make shippers jittery and raise insurance costs.With Strait of Hormuz effectively locked up by Iran and US, Red Sea had emerged as a vital alternative route, especially for energy trade out of the region.Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was working at full capacity, transporting around 7 million barrels of oil daily across the breadth of the peninsula to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This was a crucial lifeline for the global energy trade that had been severely restricted following the outbreak of the Iran war in Feb. But that East-West pipeline was hit by a drone attack last week — blamed on Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq — to coincide with the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast. Both operations seem to have been coordinated to put the choke on Red Sea shipping, which has to pass through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb strait that Houthis can now theoretically shut down.The timing of all this is not a coincidence. Actually, when the Iran war began, among Iran’s proxies in the region, Houthis held back. But in July, following the state funeral of Iran’s former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, an Iranian plane carrying the Houthi delegation back to Yemen was threatened by Saudi Arabia. Riyadh did not want that plane to land, and bombed the airport in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital of Sanaa. But that plane landed anyway.Following the episode, Houthi rhetoric against the Saudis flared up. But the key development that may have pushed Houthis into action could be the American blockade of Iranian ports and shipping in Persian Gulf.By many estimates, that blockade appears to be working, and putting enormous pressure on the Iranian economy. Tehran is unable to push out its own oil, the Iranian rial has tanked, and Iranians have actually taken to saving eggs instead of hard cash. Plus, this is a strategy that plays into America’s strength — it can carry out a naval blockade for a far longer period than a continuous kinetic war against Iran.So, Iran, through the Houthi action, is sending the message that if oil can’t pass through Hormuz, any alternative routes, including through the Red Sea, will also be shut. In short, the energy trade in the region is handcuffed till the war is resolved.What do Houthis want? The Houthis’ main grievance is against the Saudis, whom they have been fighting since 2015. But, of course, as a member of Iran’s so-called ‘Axis of Resistance’, they are now being heavily supported by Tehran in terms of material and intelligence inputs. Especially since the Gaza and Iran wars have seen Tehran’s two main proxies in Hezbollah and Hamas take a huge battering. So, the Iranian Axis appears to be undergoing a recalibration, with Houthis and Iran-backed militias in Iraq taking a more leading role among the proxies. Ultimately Houthis want legitimacy. Their attacks against Saudi Arabia — they reportedly fired a drone at Mecca earlier this week — raise their profile. Their capture of the Red Sea coast gives them international attention. And these, in turn, see them emerge as the primary force in Yemen, instead of the internationally backed Yemeni transition govt. Obviously, all of this helps Iran.Because US has refused to directly intervene against Houthis this time. Washington is providing diplomatic and advisory support to Riyadh, but not much else. Saudis want missile and drone interceptors. But US stocks are running low, thanks to its war with Iran. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has similarly sought assistance from Egypt and UK. But no one is rushing military aid to Riyadh. Interestingly, even the recently inked Mecca Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan hasn’t been activated.First, Houthis prove Iran’s Axis of Resistance is changing shape, with the Yemini militia taking a leading role. This has implications for both the Iran war, and security in Red Sea and Horn of Africa region. And second, alternative routes to Hormuz for energy transit, whether through sea or pipelines, are also not fully secure. They can be targeted by a host of Iran-backed militias in the region. This puts West Asia’s dominance in global energy supply under a serious cloud, perhaps forcing the international community to look for alternatives away from the region.
Article Summary: Yemen's houthis took over much of the country's red sea coast, threatening shipping. Red sea had emerged as an alternative to strait of hormuz in persian gulf. Houthis have been fighting a saudi-led military coalition for a decade. Move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark.

NEW DELHI: Air India Express suspended eight crew members for three months for failing to complete the mandatory post-flight declaration, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The incident took place on August 2 after the flight landed in Amritsar from Dubai.According to ANI, the crew was required to undergo the post-flight declaration within two hours of landing. However, they were delayed by 35 minutes and submitted the declaration after two hours and 35 minutes."As per the airline’s mandatory rules for testing of psychoactive substances, all crew members underwent the test, and the reports came negative," sources told ANI."The entire incident was reported to the DGCA, and the airline decided to suspend the eight crew members for three months," they added.According to DGCA rules, crew members operating international flights for Indian carriers must complete a post-flight alcohol test within two hours of landing in India, regardless of individual circumstances during that window.

Article Title: Putin tightens grip on Russian elections with anti-war opposition squeezed out
Article Text:
File photo: Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier by the Kremlin wall in Moscow

Yabloko squeezed out of national race

From war veterans to Putin allies

Opposition split over ‘smart voting’

Russia’s first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has begun with voters facing a sharply narrowed political field: the country’s only openly anti-war party has been barred from running a national list, while pro-Kremlin parties and war veterans dominate the ballot.The three-day vote, which began on Friday, will determine all 450 seats in the State Duma. President Vladimir Putin has cast the election as a demonstration of national unity and support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. Most anti-war candidates have been excluded, while the ruling United Russia party is expected to retain its dominant position.The biggest blow to the anti-war camp came in August, when Russia’s Supreme Court barred liberal Yabloko from fielding a national party list. Yabloko had positioned itself as the country’s only registered party openly opposing the war and calling for a ceasefire.Some Yabloko candidates are still contesting individual constituencies, but the ruling removed the party from the nationwide contest and left voters with fewer explicitly anti-war choices.The crackdown came after senior Yabloko figures faced prosecution and prison sentences over statements about the war.Party deputy chairman Lev Shlosberg was sentenced to 11 years in prison last month, according to the material cited by Politico.The space left by Yabloko has instead been occupied by parties that formally oppose United Russia on some issues but have backed key Kremlin policies, including the annexation of Ukrainian territories.The ballot also features more than 1,000 veterans of Russia’s war in Ukraine. Their presence reflects the Kremlin’s effort to elevate military veterans as a new political constituency.United Russia's campaign has also brought prominent pro-Kremlin figures into the spotlight. Foreign minister Sergei Lavrov appeared in a campaign advertisement alongside NHL star Alexander Ovechkin and RT chief Margarita Simonyan. Reuters separately reported that Ovechkin appeared in the video after being asked to participate.For the Kremlin, the election is not only about choosing lawmakers but also about demonstrating public support for the war. Putin has urged Russians to vote, saying the result would show that millions stand behind Russian troops and the country's stated wartime goals.With anti-war candidates largely squeezed out, parts of the Russian opposition are backing a strategy known as “smart voting” — supporting whichever candidate in a constituency is considered most capable of challenging United Russia, even if that candidate belongs to another established party.Yulia Navalnaya, widow of late opposition leader Alexey Navalny, has backed the approach, as has opposition campaigner Maxim Katz. Their argument is that the ballot remains one of the few relatively safe ways for Russians to express dissatisfaction with the Kremlin.But the strategy has divided the opposition itself. Yabloko leader Nikolay Rybakov has argued that voting for parties already represented in parliament amounts to supporting forces that have backed the crackdown on his party.
Article Summary: Three-day vote will determine all 450 seats in the state duma. President vladimir putin has cast the election as a demonstration of national unity and support for russia’s war in ukraine. Most anti-war candidates have been excluded, while the ruling united russia party is expected to retain its dominant position.

Article Title: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill: What it means and will India actually face 100% tariff
Article Text:
The Senate passed the bill 86-11 on August 7. (Photo: ANI)

What does the Russia sanctions law do?

India's Russian oil purchase

Russia Sanctions Bill: What It Means For India

What has India said?

What could a 100% tariff mean for India?

Will India actually face a 100% tariff?

What has China said

US President Donald Trump on Friday signed into law the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, giving his administration expanded powers to impose sanctions and tariffs on Russia and countries that continue significant purchases of Russian oil and gas.The White House said the law expands statutory sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions targeting Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran for five years.The legislation is significant for India because New Delhi remains one of the world's biggest buyers of Russian crude. However, the law does not automatically impose a 100% tariff on Indian goods. Instead, it creates a legal pathway for the Trump administration to impose such tariffs under specified conditions.The legislation targets Russian officials, financial institutions, defence-related networks and the country's so-called “shadow fleet” of vessels used to transport energy while circumventing Western restrictions.A key provision gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the five largest importers of Russian petroleum or natural gas, subject to conditions laid down in the law.It also includes provisions targeting countries that facilitate Russian oil sanctions evasion and extends the Iran Sanctions Act for another five years.The Senate passed the bill 86-11 on August 7, while the House of Representatives approved it 262-159 on Wednesday, sending it to Trump for his signature. The law was named after the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, a leading supporter of the legislation.India's crude sourcing pattern has changed sharply since 2022. Before the Ukraine war, Gulf countries accounted for more than 55% of India's crude supplies, while Russia's share was below 15%, according to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).Since then, India's purchases from Russia have increased substantially, while the Gulf's share has fallen below 30%.The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) estimates that between December 2022 and August 2026, China accounted for around half of Russia's crude exports, followed by India at 37%, Turkey at 5% and the European Union at 5%.Indian refiners have also secured supplies from the US, Brazil, Canada, Venezuela and African producers, but Russian crude remains a major part of India's import basket.India has repeatedly defended its Russian oil purchases, saying its energy policy is driven by the need to secure affordable and reliable supplies for its population.New Delhi said it was "monitoring further developments on this matter" and remained "firmly committed to ensuring energy security" for its people."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," the external affairs ministry said.The ministry also said India was determined to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests.Indian ambassador to the US Vinay Kwatra said: "India imports over 85% of its crude oil and around half its natural gas. Our sourcing reflects a fundamental national responsibility: looking outside our borders to secure adequate, affordable and uninterrupted energy for our people.""India is the world’s fastest-growing major economy and its third-largest energy consumer. Yet the average Indian consumes less than one-third of the global average and one-tenth of an average American. Our energy needs will, and must, grow,” Kwatra added.New Delhi has repeatedly argued that its purchases of Russian oil are driven by energy security and commercial considerations.“India should not allow US tariff threats to determine its energy policy,” GTRI said, adding that India should continue buying Russian oil as long as it remained commercially competitive and negotiate with Washington without granting unilateral trade concessions.Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI and a former trade ministry official, said the legislation was a pressure tactic against India.“The bill is a blunt and dangerous attempt to pressurise India to sign the bilateral trade agreement on one-sided terms. India buys Russian oil to secure affordable energy for 1.4 billion people, not to finance war, and these purchases have helped stabilise global supplies and prices,” he said, according to BBC.“Tariffs of up to 100% would punish Indian exporters and American consumers, disrupt trade and give the US president excessive power over major partners," he added.If the US eventually imposes steep tariffs on Indian goods under the new law, the biggest impact would be on Indian exports to the US rather than directly on the price of Russian crude.A tariff of up to 100% could make Indian products substantially more expensive in the American market and affect exporters across sectors.Higher import duties could reduce the competitiveness of Indian goods, although the actual impact would depend on the rate imposed, the products covered and how Washington implements the measure.The legislation therefore adds another layer of uncertainty to India-US trade ties, at a time when Washington and New Delhi are already negotiating a broader trade agreement, while India's dependence on Russian crude remains substantial.Not immediately. The law gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that meet specified criteria, but it does not itself impose a 100% tariff on India or China.India is particularly exposed because it remains one of the world's biggest buyers of Russian crude, while China is the largest buyer of Russian oil.The legislation also gives the president waiver authority under specified conditions, including certification to Congress that a waiver is in the national interest.This means the impact on India will depend on whether and how the Trump administration uses the new powers, as well as the eventual tariff rate, products covered and implementation timeline.The legislation is intended to increase economic pressure on Moscow by reducing the revenues Russia earns from energy exports. Supporters of the measure have argued that sanctions and tariffs can increase pressure on Russia and push it towards ending the war in Ukraine.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed the legislation, describing sanctions as an important tool to pressure Russia towards peace.Russia, however, criticised the move. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was monitoring the legislation and described additional US sanctions as “unfriendly actions”.“We are, of course, monitoring the progress of this document. It falls under the category of unfriendly actions, and of course the imposition of any additional sanctions by the US would certainly complicate efforts to find a peace settlement in Ukraine,” Peskov told reporters, according to Reuters.China has also rejected the US use of tariffs against countries buying Russian energy. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing opposed US “long-arm jurisdiction”.“China consistently opposes long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law and is not authorised by the United Nations Security Council,” Guo said.“China has always conducted normal economic and trade cooperation with countries around the world on the basis of equality and mutual benefit,” he said. “Such cooperation neither targets any third party nor is subject to interference or coercion from any third party,” Guo added.China buys more Russian crude than India, but much of its Russian energy imports are transported through pipelines across the two countries' land border.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump on friday signed into law the lindsey o graham sanctioning russia and iran act of 2026. The legislation is significant for india because new delhi remains one of the world's biggest buyers of russian crude. The law does not automatically impose a 100% tariff on indian goods.

Article Title: Iran war costs US $45.1 billion; fatalities possibly higher than 18 reported by Pentagon
Article Text:
File photo: Shredded tents, destroyed jet: Images reveal hidden scale of Iranian strikes on US Gulf bases

Human toll also under scrutiny

War’s wider costs

The human and material cost of America’s war with Iran is proving larger than previously disclosed, with the Pentagon telling Congress that the conflict has cost $45.1 billion so far, while a Washington Post report said the number of US military fatalities may also be higher than the Pentagon’s publicly reported tally.The Pentagon told lawmakers that the war had cost $43.6 billion as of September 3, with another $1.5 billion spent on additional fuel, according to CNN, citing sources familiar with the matter. The estimate does not include the cost of repairing damaged US military bases and buildings or provide a full accounting of indirect operational costs.The latest figure is higher than the Congressional Budget Office’s estimate of $38 billion through August 1. The CBO has estimated that the war could cost the US another $2 billion to $3 billion a month for as long as fighting continues.Separately, six US officials familiar with the Pentagon’s internal casualty accounting told the Washington Post that at least 22 US service members had died in the Middle East since the war began, four more than the 18 fatalities listed in the Pentagon’s public casualty database as of Friday.One official put the number at 23, saying not all of the additional deaths were directly tied to combat but involved US personnel in the region amid the ongoing hostilities. Three US contractors based in the region have also died since combat operations began, according to the report.The Pentagon declined to address questions about the discrepancy, while details surrounding the additional deaths, including the identities of those killed and when, how and where they died, remained unclear.The financial estimate also does not capture the full cost of damage to US military infrastructure. US Central Command estimated the war had cost $43.6 billion through early September, including $28 billion to replace munitions and more than $4.3 billion in lost or damaged equipment.The conflict has also put pressure on US weapons stocks and disrupted global energy markets after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis have control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The CBO said the war could push inflation 0.5 percentage points higher in the first quarter of 2027 because of higher energy prices.
Article Summary: Pentagon tells congress that the conflict has cost $45.1 billion so far. Congressional budget office estimates the war could cost the us another $2 billion to $3 billion a month for as long as fighting continues. Washington post report says number of us military fatalities may also be higher than the pentagon’s publicly reported tally.

Article Title: “If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him”: Newly minted FBI special agent Shaquille O’Neal targets Inside the NBA co-host to put behind bars in a humorous jab
Article Text:
Shaquille O'Neal targets Charles Barkley. Image via: Getty Images

Shaquille O'Neal targets Charles Barkley in his honorary FBI special agent speech

Shaquille O'Neal's law enforcement ties run back two decades

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shaquille O'Neal picked up an honorary FBI special agent title, and the four-time NBA champion wasted no time putting it to use. He graduated alongside 265 law enforcement officials at the FBI National Academy's Session 299 in Quantico, Virginia, then closed his speech with a warning aimed squarely at his longtime broadcast partner.FBI Director Kash Patel handed O'Neal the recognition once the ten-week program wrapped. O'Neal turned the moment into a shot at Charles Barkley , the co-host he has jabbed at on Inside the NBA since 2011, telling the room what to do if they ever ran into him.Shaquille O'Neal's parting line was simple. "If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him," he said, in video shared by Legion Hoops as he wrapped his remarks Thursday. The crowd of graduating officers, all veterans of their own departments, got the joke instantly given O'Neal and Barkley's decade-plus history of ribbing each other on air.Patel had announced the honor on X a day earlier, calling O'Neal "one of the best supporters of law enforcement in the country" as he presented the plaque. The title carries no real authority. It does not make O'Neal a sworn agent or give him powers of arrest, and the National Academy itself runs separately from the FBI's actual new-agent training pipeline. It exists mainly for experienced law enforcement leaders, covering leadership, academics and physical fitness over ten weeks in Quantico.This is not O'Neal dabbling. He was sworn in as a Miami Beach reserve police officer in 2005, not long after serving in the same capacity with the Los Angeles Port Police. That same year, during his reserve training, he tailed a car whose passengers had thrown a bottle at two pedestrians, then radioed dispatch so officers could track down the suspect. He later took on a reserve role in Doral, Florida, and was named Henry County Police Department's community relations chief last year.Orlando drafted him first overall in 1992, and he spent 19 seasons across six teams, winning three titles with the Lakers and one with the Heat, taking home MVP honors in 2000 and making 15 All-Star teams before his 2016 Hall of Fame induction. But the badge, honorary or not, fits a pattern he has kept up since long before Inside the NBA made him a household name twice over.As for Barkley, he has not responded publicly yet. Given their on-air history, a comeback is probably just a matter of time.
Article Summary: Shaquille o'neal picked up an honorary fbi special agent title. The four-time nba champion wasted no time putting it to use. He graduated alongside 265 law enforcement officials at the fbi national academy's session 299 in quantico, virginia. He closed his speech with a warning aimed squarely at charles barkley.
